title: The 5 Largest Moons in the Solar System, Ranked (#1 Beats a Planet)

scenes.text: The five biggest moons in the solar system, ranked. Number one is bigger than an actual planet.

scenes.label: Europa · 3,122 km
scenes.text: Number five: Europa. Three thousand one hundred and twenty-two kilometers wide, with an ocean hidden under its ice.

scenes.label: Moon · 3,475 km
scenes.text: Number four: our own Moon. About three thousand four hundred and seventy-five kilometers across, bigger than Europa.

scenes.label: Io · 3,643 km
scenes.text: Number three: Io, the most volcanic body we know. Thirty-six hundred and forty-three kilometers across.

scenes.label: Callisto · 4,821 km
scenes.text: Number two: Callisto. About forty-eight hundred kilometers wide, almost as big as the planet Mercury.

scenes.label: Ganymede · 5,268 km
scenes.text: Number one: Ganymede. Fifty-two hundred and sixty-eight kilometers wide. That is wider than the planet Mercury.

description:
The five largest moons in the solar system, ranked by diameter.
From Europa to Ganymede, the biggest moon of all, which is wider than the planet Mercury.
Which moon would you visit first?
first_comment: Which moon would you land on first? And what should we rank next?
